content:
**Largest Global Cosmetics (Beauty & Personal‑Care) Companies – Founding Years**  
*(Revenue figures reflect the most recent full fiscal year available (2023‑2024) and are shown in US‑dollar equivalents where possible. “Beauty” includes makeup, skin‑care, hair‑care, fragrance and related personal‑care categories.)*

| # | Company (Headquarters) | 2023‑24 Revenue (≈) | Year Founded | Notable Brands |
|---|------------------------|--------------------|--------------|----------------|
| 1 | **L’Oréal** (France) | **US $41 bn** (≈ €38.3 bn) | **1909** | L’Oréal Paris, Garnier, Maybelline, Lancôme, Kiehl’s |
| 2 | **Unilever – Beauty & Personal Care** (UK/Netherlands) | **US $14 bn** (beauty segment) | **1929** (Lever & Margarine merger) | Dove, Axe, Sunsilk, Pond’s, Vaseline |
| 3 | **Procter & Gamble – Beauty** (USA) | **US $14 bn** (beauty segment) | **1837** | Olay, Pantene, Head & Shoulders, SK-II (via partnership) |
| 4 | **Estée Lauder Companies** (USA) | **US $16.2 bn** (net sales) | **1946** | Estée Lauder, MAC, Clinique, Bobbi Brown, La Mer |
| 5 | **Shiseido** (Japan) | **US $8.5 bn** (≈ ¥1.19 tn) | **1872** | Shiseido, NARS, Clé de Peau Beauté, Anessa |
| 6 | **Kao Corporation** (Japan) | **US $9 bn** (≈ ¥1.3 tn) | **1887** | Jergens, Bioré, Molton Brown, Kanebo |
| 7 | **Coty Inc.** (USA) | **US $5.6 bn** (net revenue) | **1904** (as “Coty Florida”) | CoverGirl, Clairol, Max Factor, Calvin Klein Fragrances |
| 8 | **Johnson & Johnson – Consumer Health (Beauty)** (USA) | **US ≈ $7 bn** (beauty‑related) | **1886** | Neutrogena, Aveeno, Clean & Clear, Johnson’s Baby |
| 9 | **Amorepacific** (South Korea) | **US $4 bn** (≈ ₩5.3 tn) | **1945** | Laneige, Sulwhasoo, Innisfree, Etude House |
|10| **LVMH – Perfumes & Cosmetics** (France) | **US $14 bn** (beauty & fragrance division) | **1987** (LVMH group formation) | Dior, Givenchy, Guerlain, Benefit, Fenty Beauty (via Kendo) |

### How the list was compiled
* **Revenue ranking** – based on publicly disclosed 2023‑24 financial results (annual reports, Form 10‑K, and consolidated statements). For conglomerates (Unilever, P&G, J&J, LVMH) the “beauty/personal‑care” segment revenue was extracted from the segment breakdowns in those reports.  
* **Founding year** – taken from each company’s official history or reputable business reference (e.g., company websites, *Forbes*, *Statista*, *Bloomberg*).  
* **Currency conversion** – non‑USD figures were converted at the average 2023 FX rate (≈ 1 € = 1.07 USD; 1 ¥ = 0.0066 USD; 1 ₩ = 0.00075 USD) for consistency.

### Quick take‑aways
* **L’Oréal** remains the clear leader, with a market‑cap that dwarfs all peers and a heritage dating back to 1909.  
* Most of the other top players were founded **in the early‑ to mid‑20th century**, reflecting the long‑standing nature of the beauty industry.  
* **Asian giants** (Shiseido, Kao, Amorepacific) have risen into the top‑10 thanks to strong domestic markets and aggressive global expansion.  
* **Conglomerates** (Unilever, P&G, J&J, LVMH) dominate the “beauty” slice of much larger consumer‑goods portfolios, underscoring how personal‑care has become a core pillar of diversified multinational groups.  

*All figures are approximations based on the most recent audited reports available as of late 2024.*
